prompts: This is an instructional notebook. It is part of the Predictive Modeling Pipeline module of the Scikit-learn Associate Course. It introduces cross-validation as a more robust alternative to a single train-test split for estimating a model's generalization performance on the adult census dataset using only numerical features. Key learning objectives are: (1) understanding why a single train-test split is insufficient and how K-fold cross-validation addresses this by repeating the fit/score procedure across multiple data partitions; (2) building a pipeline with make_pipeline combining StandardScaler and LogisticRegression; (3) using cross_validate with cv=5 and interpreting its output dictionary, particularly test_score; (4) computing and reporting the mean and standard deviation of scores to quantify both performance and its uncertainty. Expected outputs include: data_numeric with four numerical columns, a model pipeline, cv_result dictionary with fit_time, score_time, and test_score arrays, and a printed summary of mean accuracy ± standard deviation (approximately 0.800 ± 0.003). While model.score evaluates a single already-trained model on one fixed dataset, cross_validate trains and scores the model multiple times on different data splits and internally calls the equivalent of score on each fold, yielding a more reliable and variance-aware estimate of generalization performance. Cross-validation does not produce a single deployable model; its purpose is performance estimation. If the student asks a question that cannot be answered from this context alone, refer to https://inria.github.io/scikit-learn-mooc/python_scripts/02_numerical_pipeline_cross_validation.html. If asked about more information, point the student to the video 'validation of a model' (https://skolar.probabl.ai/en/a/2533310879897316814;p=1,2592619793993357212,159767030410832489,2151018095747660947;pa=0)
